chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Khirash narrated to us, he said: My master Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, he said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: There is a gate in Paradise called 'Al-Rayyan', through which only those who fast will enter. - And this gate is called 'Al-Rayyan' because thirst exhausts the faster more than hunger does, so when the faster enters through this gate, he meets the thirst that will never quench him again.

key_terms.الرِّيَانُ: Al-Rayyan (The gate of Paradise for fasters)

ai.seo_question: What is the special gate in Paradise for those who fast?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith highlights the unique spiritual reward for fasting, emphasizing that the gate 'Al-Rayyan' is reserved exclusively for those who observe Ramadan fasts. The etymology of the name reflects the physical reality that thirst is often more acute than hunger during fasting; thus, entry through this gate grants the believer eternal satisfaction from thirst, a state of perpetual coolness and relief. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the tangible, bodily rewards of worship, linking the ascetic discipline of fasting directly to a specific, named entrance in Paradise.
